PublicEndpoint.^description: The Transfer Family server uses a public endpoint, which is reachable from the internet and cannot be restricted with security groups. Use a VPC-hosted endpoint and limit source IPs with security groups.
PublicEndpoint.shortDesc: Use a VPC endpoint instead of a public endpoint

FtpEnabled.^description: The server has the FTP protocol enabled. FTP sends credentials and data unencrypted. Use SFTP or FTPS instead.
FtpEnabled.shortDesc: Disable FTP and use SFTP or FTPS

SecurityPolicy.^description: The server uses a legacy security policy that allows older cryptographic algorithms. Switch to a current policy such as TransferSecurityPolicy-2024-01 or later. Confirm client compatibility first.

Logging.^description: The server has no logging configured. Without logs you cannot audit file transfers or investigate failed logins. Enable CloudWatch logging with a logging role or structured log destination.
Logging.shortDesc: Enable CloudWatch logging for the server

VpcSecurityGroups.^description: The VPC-hosted server has no security groups attached. Attach security groups that allow inbound access only from trusted source IPs.
VpcSecurityGroups.shortDesc: Attach security groups to the VPC endpoint

FtpsCertificate.^description: The server has FTPS enabled but no certificate is configured. FTPS requires a valid ACM certificate to encrypt connections.
FtpsCertificate.shortDesc: Attach an ACM certificate to the FTPS server

ServiceManagedIdentity.^description: The server stores users in Transfer Family (service managed). A custom identity provider such as Directory Service, Lambda or API Gateway lets you centralize authentication, enforce MFA and apply your password policy.

LoginBanner.^description: No pre-authentication login banner is configured. A banner can state acceptable use and legal notices to users before they log in, which some compliance standards require.

UserHomeDirectory.^description: Some users do not use logical home directories. Logical directories hide the real bucket or file system structure and keep users inside their own path.
UserHomeDirectory.shortDesc: Use logical home directories for users

SingleAzEndpoint.^description: The VPC endpoint is attached to a single subnet, so it is not resilient to the loss of an Availability Zone. Attach subnets in at least two Availability Zones.
SingleAzEndpoint.shortDesc: Attach subnets in multiple Availability Zones

NoUsers.^description: The server has no users but is still billed hourly for each enabled protocol. Delete it if it is no longer needed.

MultipleProtocols.^description: The server has more than one protocol enabled. Each protocol is billed hourly, so disable protocols your clients do not use.

ServerOffline.^description: The server is offline or stopped. Review whether it is still needed and delete it if not. Check the pricing page for how stopped servers are billed.

DirectoryListing.^description: Directory listing optimization is disabled on this S3-backed server. Enabling it speeds up listings of large directories.

ResourceTags.^description: The server has no tags. Tags help with cost allocation, ownership and access control.

StructuredLogging.^description: Structured JSON logging is not configured. Structured logs are easier to query and alert on than the legacy logging role format.
